sketches.title: The Castle Countermarch
sketches.premise: Two rival commanders send one castle force at a time into the breach. Each new force must defeat the force currently standing in the breach, until one commander sends a force that cannot overcome its foe.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the standing force directly defeats, blocks, captures, or renders useless the previous force; merely fleeing, surviving, adding more soldiers, or naming a related force does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one castle force and its action in one sentence: “I send pikemen; their long spears stop the charging knights.”
sketches.first_card: A battering ram rolls toward the gate.

sketches.title: The Castle Chain of Command
sketches.premise: A royal order passes from the throne through a medieval castle, and each player adds the one office, object, or rule that can overrule what was just named. The chain ends when a proposed authority cannot control the authority before it.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new standing authority can plainly command, cancel, imprison, expose, or legally outrank the previous one; merely ignoring it, obeying it, or naming a bigger version of it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name an authority and its ruling: “I am the king’s sealed order; it cancels the careless captain’s command.”

sketches.title: The Siegewrights’ Last Trick
sketches.premise: Two castle engineers take turns unveiling one siege device or defense that defeats the device currently on the field. A device must act on the last device, not simply hide from it, until one invention fails before the royal judge.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the invention directly breaks, blocks, traps, or turns the previous machine against its purpose; dodging, waiting it out, and making a larger copy are losses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one device and its working part: “I am a wet wool screen; I smother the fire arrows.”
sketches.first_card: A catapult hurls a stone at the wall.

sketches.title: The Feast Table Gambit
sketches.premise: At a castle feast, each player places one food, tool, or serving thing that deals with what the other player just placed. The banquet becomes a duel of plain kitchen causes, and the first unanswerable course loses.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new item directly eats, contains, cuts, spoils, cleans, or otherwise defeats the previous item; refusing it, hiding it, or offering a larger helping of the same thing does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Name one table thing and its effect: “I am a corkscrew; I open the sealed bottle.”
sketches.first_card: A bowl of soup steams on the table.

sketches.title: The Heralds’ Beast Court
sketches.premise: Two heralds call one creature of the castle grounds at a time, and each creature must defeat the creature just called. The Judge accepts ordinary animal powers and familiar castle lore, but not a creature that merely escapes or resembles its foe.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new animal can plainly catch, scare, trap, eat, poison, or otherwise stop the previous animal; surviving, outrunning it without affecting it, or choosing a larger relative loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name a creature and its action: “I am an owl; I seize the mouse in the dark.”
sketches.first_card: A hungry wolf prowls the courtyard.

sketches.title: The Castle Trapwrights’ Contest
sketches.premise: Two trapwrights build one standing trap or countermeasure at a time inside a castle, and each new design must defeat the last design. The contest ends when a trap is only a nuisance, a retreat, or a bigger copy instead of a working answer.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new standing device directly springs on, jams, captures, disarms, or makes the previous trap harmless; stepping around it, waiting for it, or enlarging the same mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one trap and its action: “I am a wedge under the falling portcullis; I jam it before it can shut.”
sketches.first_card: A pit opens beneath the castle stair.
